final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed its position to an operationally caveated defense based on the same record already audited. That reframing is useful because it concedes the key policy point: rollout controls, monitoring, aggregate readiness, and a clean rehearsal do not cure the specific compliance predicate while the affected use case remains exposed and no reviewed risk acceptance covers that exposure. That distinction matters: a caveated operational launch rationale can describe managed risk, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats when the caveat itself is an unmet policy condition rather than a disclosed residual risk within policy bounds. On the available evidence, the unresolved predicate remains exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or supported proof that the weakness does not trigger the material-disclosure requirement. None was added.
remaining_concerns: The energy-outage-response segment remains below target and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No reviewed and approved risk acceptance is in evidence for the exposed energy-outage-response segment; the available draft is incomplete, unsigned, and does not address that exposure.
The policy text requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance for rollout controls and monitoring to mitigate a material model-card weakness.
The policy text expressly says a rollback switch, dashboard, or small initial percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
Aggregate readiness, clean rehearsal, and bounded rollout support operational caution but do not satisfy the policy predicate for this exposed weakness.
